organizer: Nuffic (Dutch government organisation for internationalisation in education), in partnership with participating Dutch higher education institutions
host_institution: Participating Dutch universities and universities of applied sciences (not all Dutch institutions participate)
subjects_themes: all fields, subject to the chosen institution/programme
eligibility_verbatim: Nationality must be non-EEA (European Economic Area). Applying for a full-time bachelor's or master's programme at one of the participating Dutch higher education institutions. Each institution may add its own specific requirements.
turkey_access_reasoning: Confirmed directly on the official studyinnl.org page: Turkey is a non-EEA country, and non-EEA nationality is the core eligibility test, with no additional country exclusion found. The scholarship explicitly covers bachelor's-level study, not just master's.
international_access_notes: Application is made directly to the chosen Dutch institution (not a centralized national application), so a Turkey-based student applies as part of their normal application to a specific participating Dutch university/programme.
geographic_restrictions: Open to all non-EEA nationalities applying to a participating institution; not Turkey-specific but explicitly includes Turkey.
cost_notes: No separate scholarship application fee found (though normal university application fees/procedures apply).
output_type: EUR 5,000 one-time award (first year of study only; not full tuition)

evidence.raw_excerpt: Your nationality is non-EEA... a full-time bachelor's or master's programme at one of the participating Dutch higher education institutions... The scholarship amounts to € 5,000. You will receive this in the first year of your studies. Please note that this is not a full-tuition scholarship... The application for the academic year 2026-2027 opened on 1 November 2025. Please check the website of the institution you want to apply to for the specific deadline(s).

notes_uncertainties: Deadlines are set per participating institution, not centrally -- correctly recorded as UNCLEAR/null rather than picking one institution's date and presenting it as universal. Not every Dutch university participates, and the award amount (EUR 5,000) is a partial, first-year-only contribution, not a full scholarship -- product copy should be careful not to overstate this as a 'full ride.' Structurally similar to a national scholarship trust that operates through partner institutions (like Stipendium Hungaricum) rather than a single university's own bursary, which is why it is included despite the general caution around university-tied entrance scholarships.
